subject: Recap + next steps: multi-tenant controls (rate limits, quotas, routing)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@atlashealth.io>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlashealth.io>
Date: 2025-11-18T14:12:00-08:00
Subject: Recap + next steps: multi-tenant controls (rate limits, quotas, routing)

Jordan — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and suggested next steps so everyone is aligned.

Pain points you shared:
- Unpredictable per-tenant costs when a handful of accounts spike usage; need hard per-customer quotas and alerting.
- Desire to tier customers (free/pro/trial/enterprise) with distinct rate limits and latency SLOs.
- Need per-customer routing to different model variants based on tier (cheaper quantized models for lower tiers, full-precision for enterprise).
- Auditability: per-tenant request logs and token-level cost breakdowns for billing reconciliation and SOC review.
- Current stack: you run a mix of in-house inference endpoints behind an API Gateway and a custom billing layer; main concern is operational overhead during scale.

Redwood fit / what we covered:
- Per-customer quotas and burst controls (configurable by policy) and metrics that map to billing units.
- Routing policies that can send traffic to different model variants or Dedicated pools based on tenant attributes.
- Prefix/KV caching + batching recommendations to lower per-token cost for repetitive prompt patterns.
- Audit logs, token breakdowns, and export hooks for your billing/finance stack.

Success criteria you mentioned:
1) Hard per-tenant daily/monthly quota enforcement with alerting and graceful 429 handling.
2) Ability to define at least three tiered routing policies (trial/pro/enterprise) with isolated perf profiles.
3) Transparent token-level cost reports for reconciliation with finance.
4) Low-friction integration with your existing API gateway and billing system.

Proposed next steps:
- I attached a short one-pager that maps features to the success criteria (Redwood-MultiTenant-OnePager.pdf).
- Schedule a technical deep dive with our infra engineer to validate integration points and confirm performance targets. Proposed slot: 2025-11-20 10:00am PST — Monica, can you own the calendar invite?
- If the deep dive looks good, we can prepare an initial SOW + a Dedicated pilot for a subset of enterprise tenants.

Open questions for you (helps us scope the deep dive):
- Approx. daily request distribution between your top 10 tenants (ballpark is fine).
- Any regulatory constraints (data residency or logging retention limits) beyond standard HIPAA considerations?
- Do you expect to use different model families by tier, or only different quantization/instance types?

Thanks again — I’ll wait for the calendar confirmation and any answers to the above so Monica and I can prepare.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: Redwood-MultiTenant-OnePager.pdf (1 page)
Attachment: discovery-notes-20251118.txt (internal notes)
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@atlashealth.io>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlashealth.io>, legal@atlashealth.io
Date: 2025-11-18T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: multi-tenant controls (rate limits, quotas, routing)

Diego — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications:

- Daily distribution: rough split is 70% concentrated in our top 5 accounts, top account is ~40% of traffic. We can share anonymized traffic logs before the deep dive.
- Residency: all PHI must remain in us-west-2; retention for logs is currently 365 days.
- Model mapping: preference is to route lower tiers to cheaper/quantized versions of the same family, but we may route certain enterprise customers to specialized models later.

We’d like the tech deep dive. 2025-11-20 10:00am PST works for me. Priya from our infra team will join to cover the gateway/billing integration. Legal looped in for visibility re: retention and audit logs.

One ask: can you include a brief note on how throttling looks from the client side (429 behavior + recommended retry/backoff pattern)? That will help our API team.

—Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering | Atlas Health
jordan.ellis@atlashealth.io | +1 415-867-4410
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@atlashealth.io>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlashealth.io>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2025-11-18T17:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: multi-tenant controls (rate limits, quotas, routing)

Great — thanks for the answers, Jordan. Short answers to your asks:
- We’ll share an anonymized traffic sample ahead of the deep dive.
- We support region pinning for both inference and logs; can confirm retention controls during the call.
- Throttling behavior: Redwood returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. Best practice is exponential backoff with jitter; for request patterns that require guaranteed delivery we recommend a small client-side queue + non-blocking retries. I’ll paste a short example snippet in the deep-dive agenda.

Monica will send the calendar invite and a tech agenda. We’ll include a section on integration patterns (API Gateway, webhooks for billing, and S3 export for logs).

Diego

On a separate note — Priya, if you can share the current billing export format (CSV columns) that’ll help map our token breakdown to your invoices.
